page.layout: One page of text in verse lines, with a left margin of short notes beside the verse; running head at top; page number at top left. Below the text, the final word "Hos" is set at the right as a catchword.

p.i: Impastus carpat si membra iacentia vultur.
Barbara nunc patriis vlulantem carmina linguis,
Ad numerum resonas gaudentem plaudere cetras.
Segne viris,quicquid duro sine Marte gerendum est,
Extractum lustris primo Viriatthus in auo
Nomen Romanis suetum mox nobile damnis.
Aut Vasco insuetus galea,ferre arma morati.
Nec qua Dardanios post vidit Ilerda furores,
Nec qui Massagetem monstrans feritate parentem
Iamq; Ebusus Phoenissa mouet,mouet Artabrus arma,
Iam cui Tlepolemus sator,& cui Lyndus origo,
Feruida bella ferens Balearis,& alite plumbo.
Et quos nunc Grauia violato nomine Graium,
Dat Carthago viros Teucro fundata vetusto.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the left are short place and people labels, transcribed as printed. Some Greek letters in the verse are rendered as close approximations; the word "Hos" at the foot is the catchword. Several letters in the scan are doubtful, including the notes' abbreviations and the Greek-name forms.
